solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Trite description of Wimbledon maybe?

definitions.meaning: Wimbledon Common is an open space in south-west London, so Wimbledon could be called a place with a common

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a dull way of describing the famous tennis venue.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon suggests tennis, but the second reading needs Wimbledon Common, a large public heath in south-west London; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something trite is everyday and unoriginal, as is a stock remark.

clue.text: Tom's seen by hospital in visit covering several eventualities

indicators.note: seen by means placed next to, so the pieces are joined end to end

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: in means the hospital letter goes inside the word for visit

parts.note: to call on someone is to visit them

explanation.surface: A cat is spotted visiting a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a catch-all provision is designed to cover every possible case.

clue.text: Fancy writing about school's figures of speech

indicators.note: about means the first pieces go round the school, as a container

parts.note: 'My!' is an exclamation like 'Fancy that!'
Eton is the famous English public school
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Elaborate prose about a school is described as full of rhetorical devices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective or anagram signal, but here it is the exclamation of surprise, as in 'Fancy that!'. Eton is England's best-known boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a metonym, such as 'the Crown' for the monarch, is one kind of figure of speech.

clue.text: Depose head of old car plant

indicators.note: deposing the head removes the leading letter of the following word

parts.note: Morris was a British car make, now defunct

explanation.surface: A call to oust the boss of an obsolete car factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'car plant' reads as a factory, but 'plant' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: orris is a kind of iris, a garden plant whose root is used in perfume.

clue.text: Climbing mountain's extremely nasty at first for troops

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
extremely means too, as in too much

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Scaling the peak is very unpleasant initially for the soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective: a platoon is a small military unit of troops.

clue.text: Soldiers back field marshal

indicators.note: back means the soldiers' letters are read in reverse

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of soldiers
a range is a field or area of activity, as in range of interests

explanation.surface: Troops support their top army commander, a field marshal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'field marshal' reads as a rank, but splits: 'field' is RANGE and 'marshal' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to marshal things is to set them out in order.

clue.text: Always eats food by one French chef

indicators.note: eats means the word for always takes the other pieces inside

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always
scoff is British slang for food
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone forever consumes the dishes of a single Gallic cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eats' suggests dining, but is the container signal; 'by' merely sets one piece beside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Auguste Escoffier was the celebrated French chef and culinary writer.

clue.text: So the listener's disgusted

indicators.note: the listener's version means how the word sounds when heard

parts.note: sick means disgusted, as in sick of it

explanation.surface: An audience member is revolted, so it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin: sic means thus or so, used to mark a quoted error.

clue.text: Iron Maiden shoot off touring

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the rearranged letters surround the maiden
off means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: The heavy metal band Iron Maiden film a shoot while on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns SHOOT into SOOTH, and 'touring' puts M inside it. Iron Maiden reads as the band, but 'Iron' is the verb defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to iron clothes is to press them flat and smooth.

clue.text: On the whole, college for Mark is pricey

indicators.note: college for Mark means one letter replaces the other

parts.note: on the whole means mostly, generally
M is the abbreviation for the German mark currency

explanation.surface: Overall, university education costs a lot in German money.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something pricey costs a lot of money.

clue.text: Instructor knocked back cheap booze? Not good

indicators.note: not good means the letter for good is dropped
knocked back means turned round, so the word reads in reverse

parts.note: rotgut is cheap, rough alcohol

explanation.surface: A teacher downed some cheap liquor, which was no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking, but reverses ROTGUT into TUGTOR; removing G leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a tutor is a private teacher or instructor.

clue.text: Very poor actor cast with one semi-famous

indicators.note: cast means thrown into a new shape, signalling rearranged letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: semi means half, so only the back half of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A dreadful performer gets a role alongside a minor celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like theatre casting but signals the anagram ATROC.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: atrocious work is dreadful, of very low quality.

clue.text: Employees will get depressed very easily

parts.note: hands are workers or employees, as in farm hands
down means depressed or gloomy

explanation.surface: Staff will become gloomy with very little effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: winning without effort, as a jockey wins without urging the horse with the hands.

clue.text: What a time being submerged by river could be?

definitions.text: What a time being submerged by river could be?

indicators.note: being submerged by means going inside the river's letters

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall

explanation.surface: Asks what a spell under water in a river might prove to be.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: being held under a river could kill you. The Fal is a river in Cornwall, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Consequence: drowning, staying submerged too long, can be deadly.

clue.text: Nothing's being broadcast after light satire

indicators.note: after places the light piece ahead of what comes after it

parts.note: a lamp is a light
O is zero, nothing
on means being broadcast, as in on air

explanation.surface: No satire is going out on air after the lighter material.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a lampoon is a satirical attack mocking a person.

clue.text: Old fellow put on tyre for free? It's part of the service

indicators.note: free means loosed from order, signalling rearranged letters

explanation.surface: An elderly man fits a tyre without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' sounds like no charge but tells you to rearrange 'tyre for'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the offertory is the stage of a church service when gifts are offered.

clue.text: Departure lounge's close by it

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

parts.note: X stands for by, as in multiplication: 2 by 3

explanation.surface: An airport departure lounge sits near the way out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an exit is a departure or leaving.

clue.text: Massive jerk's after private gain, I let slip

indicators.note: after means the jerk piece follows the others

parts.note: a GI is an American private soldier

indicators.note: let slip means lose, so the letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: A huge idiot is after personal profit, which I let slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' looks like an insult but is a twitch; GAN is 'gain' with I lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: gigantic and massive both mean enormous in size.

clue.text: Pants, taking run among trees

indicators.note: among puts the run letter inside the trees

parts.note: beeches are trees
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone panting as they jog through woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' reads as a verb for breathing hard, but it is the noun for trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: breeches are trousers, which pants means in American usage.

clue.text: Part of Niagara Falls reflected at a distance

indicators.note: reflected means mirrored, so the letters are read backwards
part of means the letters are taken from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A section of the waterfall appears mirrored in the water from far away.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: afar means far off, at a distance.

clue.text: Dashing off a riff's hard

indicators.note: off means wrong or out of place, signalling rearranged letters

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Playing a guitar riff fast and difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dashing' looks like rushing off, but is the adjective defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: raffish means jaunty and rakish, a dashing style.

clue.text: Row about stray dog

indicators.note: about means the row goes round the stray piece

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out over a stray dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel, but it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a terrier is a small breed of dog.

clue.text: Eccentric poet gets hold of recipe to cook fish

indicators.note: gets hold of means the rearranged letters wrap round the recipe letter
eccentric means odd, signalling rearranged letters

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe, take
to do food is to cook it

explanation.surface: An odd poet acquires a recipe for preparing fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' rearranges POET to TOPE, which takes in R.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a torpedo is a fish, the electric ray.

clue.text: Person everyone describes as nit-picking type, for starters?

definitions.text: Person everyone describes as nit-picking type, for starters?

indicators.note: for starters means the opening letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: Someone whom all call a fusspot, to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials of the first six words spell the answer, and the clue as a whole also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a pedant is a fussy stickler for detail.

clue.text: Awe possibly secured by church hat

indicators.note: secured by means held inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Loch Awe is a Scottish lake, so awe could be a loch

explanation.surface: Reverence perhaps is ensured by a church hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awe' reads as wonder but is Loch Awe, a lake in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a cloche is a close-fitting bell-shaped woman's hat.

clue.text: Well-spoken mathematician

indicators.note: spoken means said aloud, so the word is used as heard

parts.note: an oiler is an oil well, a productive well

explanation.surface: Describes an articulate maths expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-spoken' reads as articulate, but splits into the well and the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Leonhard Euler was the great Swiss eighteenth-century mathematician.

clue.text: Adversary keeps playing truant — that's lucky

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the enemy wraps round the rest

parts.note: a foe is an adversary

indicators.note: playing means moving about, signalling rearranged letters

explanation.surface: An enemy keeps skipping school, which is a stroke of luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing truant' reads as skipping school, but 'playing' is the anagram signal, giving RTUNAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: fortunate means lucky.

clue.text: Range of paintings left by Frenchman

indicators.note: left by means abandoned by, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: murals are wall paintings
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a Frenchman

explanation.surface: A collection of artworks bequeathed by a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' looks like a selection of paintings but is a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Urals are a mountain range in Russia.

clue.text: One fluked it, meeting European recluse

parts.note: an anchor has flukes, the barbed points of its arms

explanation.surface: Someone who scraped a lucky win meets a European hermit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluked' suggests luck but means having flukes, as an anchor does.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an anchorite is a religious hermit who lives in seclusion.

clue.text: A long letter…

parts.note: to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: A lengthy piece of correspondence, continued in the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Spelling: the name of the eighth letter of the alphabet, H, is written this way.

clue.text: … one giving support

parts.note: a golf peg holds the ball up before driving, and the follow-on from the previous clue makes it also a letter

explanation.surface: Continues the previous clue: a letter from someone offering help.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a golf tee holds up the ball, and the word also names the letter T.

clue.text: So there is bile chiefly in derogatory statement about search engine?

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the statement

parts.note: Yahoo is a web search engine, and saying it sucks is derogatory

indicators.note: chiefly takes the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Bile shows mainly in a rude remark about an internet search site.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a childish taunt meaning so there, expressing scorn.
